question: Parts of which present state had evolved a local system of canal irrigation called 'kulhs' over 400 years ago?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Himachal Pradesh has a unique traditional irrigation system known as 'kulhs'.
 
• Kulhs are small, perennial streams diverted from natural flowing water bodies to supply water to the fields.
 
• This irrigation system has been in use for over 400 years.
 
• It reflects the indigenous knowledge and sustainable water management practices of the region.
 
• Farmers in the region rely on kulhs for irrigation, especially in hilly terrains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Traditional Irrigation Systems:**

 
 
• Different regions in India have developed their own traditional irrigation systems such as tanks, wells, and stepwells.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Water Management:**
 
 
• Traditional systems like kulhs are examples of sustainable water management, ensuring efficient use of water resources in agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Community Participation:**
 
 
• Maintenance and management of kulhs involve active community participation, ensuring shared responsibility among farmers.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture:**
 
 
• Kulhs have significantly boosted agricultural productivity in the hilly regions by providing a reliable source of irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Modern-Day Relevance:**
 
 
• Despite advancements in irrigation technology, traditional systems like kulhs are still relevant and are being revived for their ecological and economic benefits.
